title: Vermont AI Laws

reading.body:
Vermont's only AI-related law governs synthetic media in elections, not AI systems themselves. S0023, passed March 10, 2026, requires disclosure on deceptive synthetic media published within 90 days before a Vermont election, with format rules for images, video, and audio, penalties for knowing violations, and enforcement by the Attorney General and State's Attorneys.

The pattern is narrow and procedural. The law targets a specific harm, electoral deception in a defined window, and assigns it a specific remedy, a disclosure label. It does not regulate model training, data centers, or the compute that produces synthetic media. Candidates can seek injunctive relief, which puts the response in court rather than in a technical standard.

For AI specifically, this says little about the infrastructure constraints that shape scaling. A disclosure requirement on outputs does not touch power procurement, building timelines, or grid interconnection, and nothing in the data connects it to them. One law in one state is also too thin to show a trend.

What the data does not cover: it does not say how the law is enforced in practice, whether any case has been brought, or what penalties amount to. It does not include failed bills, executive orders, or local rules. The count of one reflects this site's judgment of relevance, not a census of every Vermont statute that mentions AI.

Vermont has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Vermont

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • S0023: An act relating to the use of synthetic media in elections passed 2026-03-10

    This act requires a disclosure on synthetic media that is deceptive and fraudulent when published, communicated, or distributed within 90 days before an election in Vermont. It sets specific format requirements for the disclosure in images, video, and audio, and provides penalties for knowing and intentional violations. It also gives enforcement and investigation powers to the Attorney General and State's Attorneys, and allows candidates to seek injunctive relief.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Vermont. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
